AARON MASON.name: Aaron B. Mason
AARON MASON.background: Superior Court judge, Clayton Judicial Circuit, appointed by Gov. Nathan Deal on Dec. 19, 2016 to a new fifth judgeship created by HB 804; previously Clayton County State Court judge (appointed by Gov. Sonny Perdue, July 2010; served 2010-2017). Earlier a senior assistant attorney general for Georgia and a senior assistant solicitor general in Clayton County. AARON MASON.record: Re-elected unopposed in 2018 and 2022. Lost his May 19, 2026 re-election bid to Deitra Burney-Butler (45.2%). AJC reported that on Sept. 15, 2026 his handgun discharged at an Athens restaurant; he told police it went off accidentally while reaching for his wallet; no charges had been filed and police were investigating possible reckless conduct.

WILLIE LOCKETTE.name: Willie E. Lockette
WILLIE LOCKETTE.background: Superior Court judge, Dougherty Judicial Circuit (Albany), 1996-2024; chief judge from 2009. Began his legal career in 1974 as a staff attorney at the Albany regional office of Georgia Legal Services Programs. Appointed associate magistrate judge in Dougherty County in 1991 and chief magistrate in 1993. Won the Superior Court seat in 1996 (first African American since Reconstruction to win a contested countywide election there and first to win a Dougherty Superior Court seat by election) and was re-elected unopposed for six more terms. Has also served by designation on the Supreme Court of Georgia. Nominated in 2020 for a Supreme Court vacancy but declined to seek it. Did not seek an eighth term in 2024; term ended December 2024; applied to become a senior judge.
WILLIE LOCKETTE.record: Chief judge of the Dougherty Superior Court from 2009 to 2024; retirement celebration in December 2024 included letters from Gov. Brian Kemp, Sen. Raphael Warnock, Rep. Sanford Bishop and President Biden.
WILLIE LOCKETTE.notes: Retired at end of 2024. WALB's Dec. 2024 story says he was chief judge for 27 years, conflicting with WALB's 2020 and Jan. 2024 stories (chief judge since 2009); 2009 is used.
